hook: AI that edits AI, a $2.7B buyout and a lawsuit over scraping
summary: MIT shows a large model can edit a small model's weights directly, sharply lifting its math scores without retraining.
Salesforce buys Cresta for $2.7B; Huawei's next AI chip reportedly depends on Samsung and SK Hynix memory.
Anthropic bars Claude Code from cloning existing games, and four US papers sue Brave over AI scraping.

stories.headline: MIT researchers show LLMs can read and edit neural network weights without retraining
stories.summary: MIT’s CSAIL team demonstrated that a large language model (GPT‑6 Astra) can examine and modify a neural network’s weights directly, improving a small language model by changing only 0.016% of its parameters. In experiments the model raised the MATH‑500 score from 7.9% to 48.1% and GSM8K from 13.8% to 67.1%.
stories.why_it_matters: It shows a way to fix or enhance AI models without costly retraining, opening new debugging and optimization pathways.
source_titles: MIT Researchers Show LLMs Can Read and Edit Neural Network Weights Without Retraining
MIT Researchers show LLMs can edit neural network weights without training: Here’s what it means
Can AI fix another AI's brain? MIT researchers use GPT-6 Astra to boost Qwen's maths skills
stories.line: An LLM rewired a small model's weights directly, no retraining needed
stories.detail: MIT CSAIL changed 0.016% of the parameters and lifted MATH-500 from 7.9% to 48.1%.

stories.headline: Salesforce to acquire Cresta for $2.7 billion
stories.summary: Salesforce announced a definitive agreement to buy Cresta, an AI‑powered contact‑center automation provider, for $2.7 billion. The deal is slated to close in the first quarter of Salesforce’s fiscal 2028, pending regulatory approval.
stories.why_it_matters: The acquisition adds voice‑first AI automation to Salesforce’s Service Cloud, expanding AI capabilities for customer‑service teams.
source_titles: Salesforce announces plans to acquire Cresta, a provider of AI-powered contact center automation software; source: Salesforce agreed to pay $2.7B for Cresta (The Information)
Salesforce Adds Cresta to the Cart in Its 2026 CX Shopping Spree
Salesforce Agrees to Buy Cresta for Voice-Led Customer Service AI
stories.line: Salesforce is paying $2.7B for contact-center AI startup Cresta
stories.detail: Cresta's voice-first automation joins Service Cloud; the deal should close in Salesforce's fiscal Q1 2028.

stories.headline: Anthropic adds rule to stop Claude Code from cloning existing video games
stories.summary: Anthropic updated Claude Code’s system prompt to forbid recreating specific games, adding a rule that allows only original or genre‑based games. The change was first spotted on Oct 27 and confirmed by engineer Addy Osmani.
stories.why_it_matters: It aims to protect game developers’ intellectual property and limit AI‑driven game cloning.
source_titles: Anthropic clamps down on Claude’s AI video game clones
Claude’s new rules against game cloning won’t stop the AI copying boom
Anthropic adds rule to stop Claude Code recreating existing games
stories.line: Claude Code's new system prompt rules out cloning existing games
stories.detail: Original and genre-inspired games are still allowed. The change was first spotted on Oct 27.

stories.headline: Huawei says Ascend 960DT AI chip will use Samsung and SK Hynix HBM
stories.summary: Huawei told some customers that a large share of its upcoming flagship AI chip, Ascend 960DT, will be equipped with high‑bandwidth memory from Samsung and SK Hynix, which is being smuggled into China via board‑packaging loopholes.
stories.why_it_matters: It shows how U.S. export controls are being bypassed and that Chinese AI hardware still depends on foreign memory components.
source_titles: Sources: Huawei told some clients that a large share of its upcoming flagship AI chip, Ascend 960DT, will run largely on HBM made by Samsung and SK Hynix (The Information)
Smugglers funnel Korea's HBM to China for Huawei via server chip loophole
Chinese Smugglers Sneak South Korean HBM Chips Into China Calling It 'Patriotism' — How Do They Do It?
stories.line: Huawei's next flagship AI chip leans on Korean memory
stories.detail: Most memory for the Ascend 960DT is Korean-made, routed into China through a packaging loophole, per reports.

stories.headline: New York Times and other papers sue Brave over AI scraping and paywall bypass
stories.summary: The New York Times, New York Daily News, Chicago Tribune and Orlando Sentinel have filed lawsuits in Manhattan federal court accusing Brave Software of illegally scraping their journalism, providing it to AI companies and enabling users to bypass paywalls. The complaints allege that Brave’s “Brave Index” contains more than 30 billion web pages and that the company sold access to AI firms such as Anthropic, Perplexity, Mistral, xAI and Cohere.
stories.why_it_matters: The case highlights how AI training data practices can clash with copyright law and could shape future rules for using web content in AI models.
source_titles: The New York Times sues Brave web browser for AI scraping and bypassing paywalls
New York Times sues maker of Brave web browser over copyrights
New York Times and three other US papers sue Brave over AI scraping
stories.line: Brave faces lawsuits from the NYT and three other newspapers
stories.detail: They allege its search index scraped their journalism, sold access to AI firms and helped readers skip paywalls.
